summary.intent: Execute Phase 70.1 (rotation read-plane durability and crash-resume soundness) end-to-end: run parallel worktree execution of 13 plans, resolve the desktop-e2e D-16 acceptance checkpoint, verify the phase goal, then ship it through the full verify/secure/validate/simplify/e2e/CodeRabbit/PR pipeline.
summary.outcome: All 13 plans merged; multiple genuine product bugs (depth-3 decrypt-before-dirtiness-check, floor-store multi-writer race, desktop revocation bypass, publish double-counting, macOS idle-mount publish stall, TS checkpoint-GC premature deletion) were found and fixed across both TS and Rust rotation engines; D-16 desktop-e2e acceptance went green on macOS/Linux/Windows; phase verification passed 7/8 (SC#6 closed via live sdk-e2e run); PR #598 opened and CodeRabbit/Greptile findings triaged and fixed, with CI fixes for SC#6 grep-gate and Windows cfg gating applied.

repo: Desktop rotation uses two divergent write paths: fuser (macOS/Linux, delete.rs) and WinFsp (Windows, split set_delete→cleanup) — fixes must be ported to both or added as shared functions to avoid drift.

macOS FUSE-T defers file release ~40s and the publish queue is edge-triggered with no wall-clock backstop, so an idle mount after a write never republishes the parent folder — needed both a harness nudge and a background pump fix.

CI does not run `cargo fmt --check`, so running `cargo fmt` locally before commit only introduces version-skew churn against already-passing code; better to avoid whole-crate/workspace fmt entirely and only fmt touched files with -p scoping.
`cargo fmt -p <crate>` (not `--all`) is required or unrelated files get reformatted (drift) and block worktree merges (`worktree_dirty`).
The SC#6 grep gate (rotation transport sanctioning) requires the `// sc6-allow:` marker on the line directly above the sanctioned call — no multi-line comment gap allowed.
grant_scope.rs test modules must use `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "fuse"))]` (not bare `#[cfg(test)]`) when referencing `test_support`, or the Windows/winfsp-only cargo test job fails with E0433.
The gsd commit helper can report `commit_failed` as a false negative even when the commit lands — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL; PR body must be patched via `gh api -X PATCH .../pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.

rust-analyzer diagnostics (E0063, dead_code, unused import) frequently go stale mid-edit during background agent work; always confirm with authoritative `cargo check`/`cargo test` before trusting them.
The release-please bot pushes a `chore(release)` commit after PR open / passing Release Preview — always fetch+rebase before the next push.

code.finding: collectDirtyFrontier must check childPub.generation > childRef.generation BEFORE calling unsealChildReadKey — decrypting a dirty edge with the parent's current key throws before dirtiness is ever checked.
Rust twin of the same decrypt-before-dirtiness-check bug; must reorder check-then-decrypt identically.

Each JsonSidecarFloorStore::new() previously built its own Arc<Mutex<()>>, so multiple instances over the same sidecar path raced on a shared deterministic .tmp rename path (ENOENT). Fixed via a process-global path-keyed lock registry (shared_lock_for).

rotate_read_on_scope_exit discarded the RotateReadResult (Ok(_) match) and never refreshed the grant-root inode's in-memory read_key, so a subsequent metadata relink resealed under the stale old key — a revocation bypass. Fixed via refresh_grant_root_read_key.

build_scope_exit_child_override failed open per-child (missing inode → continue; build_child_refs error → warn+skip) unlike its fail-closed sibling build_folder_metadata, causing silent orphaning of sibling children in the coalesced republish. Fixed to propagate errors and fail closed to EIO.

Skipped-branch resume path only kept `.frontier` from verify_subtree_clean, discarding `is_dirty`, so a missing root (is_dirty:true, empty frontier) was mis-marked Complete instead of falling through to the fail-closed dirty-resume path.

repairDirtyNode called deleteWrappedKey (checkpoint GC) immediately on every repaired child, even when the parent's batched republish hadn't committed yet (pendingChildCount>1) — a crash in that window permanently lost the checkpoint. Ported the Rust twin's deferred pendingCheckpointNodeIds design to fix.

Added a background 'fuse-publish-pump' thread (2s interval, unique-name lookups to defeat SMB negative-lookup cache) as a wall-clock backstop for the edge-triggered publish-queue drain; bounded to mount lifetime via an AtomicBool.

workflow: When running wave-based parallel worktree execution, dispatch all plans in a wave truly concurrently (one Agent call per message to avoid git worktree-add lock races) rather than canary-testing one plan first — user explicitly corrected this approach.
Batch multiple cross-platform fixes (e.g. WinFsp port + macOS pump) before pushing, to avoid burning repeated ~15-40min real-mount CI cycles.
For CI failures, always distinguish infra flake (e.g. Windows DLL_INIT_FAILED, macOS FUSE-T slowness) from genuine regressions by reading actual failure logs before re-running or fixing code.

Route substantive/security-critical review findings (CodeRabbit critical/major) to an adversarial verification sub-agent before applying fixes, since CodeRabbit's stated root cause can be partially wrong even when the underlying defect is real.
When a background debugger agent claims a wrong branch or stale diagnostics, verify authoritatively (git status/cargo check) before trusting or discarding its report.

friction: Multiple rounds of stale rust-analyzer diagnostics (E0063 missing field, dead_code, unused imports) that looked like real compile errors but were mid-edit snapshots, requiring repeated authoritative cargo check/test verification.
cargo fmt --all (or unscoped fmt) repeatedly introduced out-of-scope drift across unrelated files, blocking worktree merges and requiring manual revert/discard.

Desktop-e2e CI required multiple full round-trips (each ~15-40 min) to iteratively surface layered failures: Part A setup timeout → double-publish/revocation bypass → WinFsp parity gap → macOS idle-mount stall → checkpoint-GC bug found by CodeRabbit review.
Windows CI failed once on an unrelated transient STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED runner flake before Step 8 even ran, requiring a job-specific re-run.
gsd commit helper repeatedly reported false-negative commit_failed messages, requiring manual git log verification each time.
2 orphaned rust-analyzer processes (one from a deleted stale worktree checkout, ~5.4GB) were silently leaking RAM alongside a dangling Phase-69 Claude Code session.
Long-running commits with lint-staged/eslint hooks occasionally exceeded the 120s Bash timeout, requiring status checks and higher-timeout retries.
open_items: ROT-04: desktop query_grants_rooted_at is a no-op, so a scope-exit rotation currently de-authorizes all recipients rather than selectively re-minting inner grants (sanctioned deferral, tracked as todo).
WinFsp handle_rename has an ungated overwritten dest_ino removal (D-15d parity gap) — delete path closed, rename path still open (tracked as todo).

macOS FUSE-T cross-client-sync Test 5 (content sync) and Test 7 (folder rename sync) remain soft-skipped due to FUSE-T ignoring inval_inode and serving stale SMB-cached content — logged as a new todo (2026-07-09), explicitly distinct from the write-side publish pump fix.

queue.rs has duplicated floor-sidecar skip logic (8 lines copy-pasted in load_all_for_vault and gc_failed_entries) — flagged by simplify review as low-value duplication, deferred rather than refactored.

2 tee-republish.test.ts failures during the sdk-e2e gate run were classified as pre-existing local-stack precondition issues (TEE worker not initialized) rather than phase regressions — not fixed, just noted in PR.

Dangling Phase-69 checkout directory and its associated Claude Code session were identified as stale; the RA process and session were killed, but user should confirm whether the cipher-box-phase69 directory itself should be deleted.
